audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Teemo five of seven stages (win = Teemo, Teemo, Teemo, Skill, Teemo, Skill, Teemo) in a lane Malphite wins 52.97% over 2475 games, and it contradicts the entry's own text: whys[4] calls Level 6 'your spike', whys[5] says 'force every all-in now', whys[6] says 'You still win the duel outright'. All three sit under a stage the chart awards to Teemo.
audit.why: The mirror reached the same conclusion from the other side: audits/top/teemo__malphite.json records Teemo at 48.33% and says its own chart needs redrawing for the same reason. Levels 1-3 are genuinely Teemo's — Blinding Dart on a flat 7s blanks the autos Malphite's whole trade runs on. From Level 6 the lane is Malphite's.
audit.corrected: Teemo owns Levels 1-3. Level 6 onward is Malphite's: no dash means Unstoppable Force always connects, and Ground Slam's attack-speed cut is a hard answer to an attack-speed damage profile.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] and wants.you[2] make the first-item spike 'stack armor (Iceborn/Sunfire)' to 'blank his on-hit DPS'. The full layer of the same matchup lists 'Build armor vs his AP' as a critical DON'T.
audit.why: Toxic Shot is magic damage. Armour reduces none of it, so as a defensive purchase against Teemo it does nothing — and the two layers currently tell the player opposite things. Armour is still worth buying, but for the reason neither layer gives: Ground Slam's damage is calculated from Malphite's Armor, so every armour item is an offensive item here. What actually blanks his on-hit engine is Ground Slam's attack-speed reduction on a flat 7s, because his damage is attack-speed driven.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam's attack-speed cut is the answer to Toxic Shot, not armour. Armour is offensive (it scales Ground Slam); MR is the defensive buy against an all-magic kit.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (E: magic damage based on his Armor, reduces Attack Speed, cd 7)

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet-flagged: the entry names none of Teemo's abilities — everything is 'his blind (Q)', 'E poison', 'shrooms', 'passive move speed'. Separately, early tells the player that stepping out of auto range between trades refreshes Granite Shield and 'soaks most of his poke'.
audit.why: That last line is the load-bearing error. Granite Shield only recharges after Malphite has gone a few seconds without being hit, and Toxic Shot poisons on impact and then ticks every second for four seconds afterwards. One auto suppresses the shield for the whole poison duration, so walking out of range does not bring it back — the poison clock has to expire first. The advice as written tells the player he has a reset he does not have. The mirror entry is built around the same interaction from Teemo's side.
audit.corrected: Toxic Shot ticks for four seconds after the hit, and Granite Shield needs a few seconds unhit to recharge — so a single auto keeps your shield off through the whole DoT. Names: Guerrilla Warfare (P), Blinding Dart (Q, flat 7s, 680), Move Quick (W, 14s), Toxic Shot (E), Noxious Trap (R).
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (E Toxic Shot: 'damage on impact and each second after for 4 seconds')

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states what Blinding Dart does and does not stop. spikes[1] says Unstoppable Force 'lands point-blank with no dodge', which is right, but never says why it survives the blind.
audit.why: Blinding Dart blanks basic attacks. That is devastating against Thunderclap, which is an auto-attack reset whose aftershocks ride on the next few attacks — one dart erases the whole window rather than a single hit. It does nothing to Unstoppable Force, Seismic Shard or Ground Slam. Saying so converts a vague 'bait the blind' into a rule: never open with autos, always open with R.
audit.corrected: Blinding Dart stops basic attacks only, so it eats Thunderclap's whole aftershock window but never touches Unstoppable Force, Seismic Shard or Ground Slam. Flat 7s at every rank, 680 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: late warns about facechecking brush but never mentions Guerrilla Warfare, and Noxious Trap is only ever 'shrooms'.
audit.why: Guerrilla Warfare is why the brush is dangerous: standing still makes him invisible indefinitely, and inside brush he keeps the invisibility while moving. That is a different threat from a ward-able champion sitting in a bush. Noxious Trap slows and poisons over time — it is the zoning tool that stops Malphite ever walking a fight down.
audit.corrected: Guerrilla Warfare makes him invisible while still, and lets him stay invisible while moving inside brush. Noxious Trap slows and poisons — it is a zoning tool, not a displacement.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (P Guerrilla Warfare; R Noxious Trap)

edits.before: Teemo owns the opening. His blind (Q) cancels the empowered autos of your Thunderclap and his passive move speed means you can't walk him down, so don't waste mana throwing a Seismic Shard at max range hoping to chase — just last-hit and accept the E-poison chip. Your Granite Shield passive is the saving grace: step out of his auto range between trades and the shield refreshes, soaking most of his poke. Don't flame your jungler; this is a survive-to-6 lane, not a level-2 cheese.
edits.after: Teemo owns the opening. Blinding Dart (Q) is a flat 7s from 680 and it blanks basic attacks, which means it eats Thunderclap's entire aftershock window rather than one hit, while Move Quick (W) means you cannot walk him down. The trap to avoid: Granite Shield does NOT reset just because you stepped back. Toxic Shot (E) ticks every second for four seconds after the hit, and the shield only recharges once you have gone a few seconds unhit — so one auto keeps it off you for the whole poison. Last-hit, take the chip, reach 6.

edits.before: This is where it flips. The instant you hit 6, Unstoppable Force gives you something Teemo cannot answer — he has no dash, no flash-tier escape, so a well-timed R from brush or fog locks him for a full Thunderclap + Ground Slam combo. Bait the blind first: trade a Seismic Shard so he burns Q, then R in on the cooldown. With your first armor item, Ground Slam's attack-speed slow guts his on-hit damage and your Granite Shield outlasts his poke. Hold R for when his Q is down.
edits.after: This is where it flips. At 6, Unstoppable Force gives you something Teemo cannot answer: he has no dash, and Blinding Dart stops basic attacks only, so your R connects through it from fog or brush and locks him for Thunderclap and Ground Slam. Open with R, never with autos — the blind is a flat 7s and it is worth more to him than any single hit. Ground Slam's attack-speed cut, also a flat 7s, is the item-independent answer to his on-hit poison. Hold R for the seconds after Blinding Dart is spent.

edits.before: You win every straight 1v1 he's foolish enough to take — he can't out-burst your armor and he can't escape your R. But Teemo stops fighting you and becomes a map problem: shrooms wall off every choke and objective pit, and his splitpush exploits your zero waveclear pressure and low mobility. Use your R as a flank/engage on his carries in fights rather than chasing the rat, and never facecheck unswept brush near Baron or Dragon — one shroom chunk before a fight is how he claws value back.
edits.after: You win every straight 1v1 he takes — no dash means no escape from R, and Ground Slam's attack-speed cut guts an attack-speed damage profile. But Teemo stops fighting you and becomes a map problem: Noxious Trap slows and poisons every choke and pit, and Guerrilla Warfare makes him invisible standing still, and invisible while moving inside brush. Use R as a flank on his carries rather than chasing him, and never facecheck unswept brush near Baron or Dragon.

notes: MIRROR: reused audits/top/teemo__malphite.json — the Granite-Shield-versus-poison interaction, Ground Slam as the hard counter to an attack-speed damage profile, and the armour/magic itemisation error.
